summary: A narrator recalls a conversation in which a man (Alex Goddard, apparently) explains how Sarah came to Quetzal Manor in New York seeking a divine, virginal pregnancy through 'cosmic energy.' He reveals Sarah had a rare uterine abnormality, that she refused to give up, and that she wanted to come to Baalum, the place of miracles, under an agreement he regretted offering. The narrator also reflects on a childhood memory of Sarah's questions about how babies are born and on her own parallel search for a miracle.
one_line: Book 3, part 132: Alex Goddard explains Sarah's troubled quest for a miraculous pregnancy and her insistence on traveling to Baalum.
key_facts: Sarah first appeared at Quetzal Manor in New York as a very troubled young woman.
Sarah declared she was a person of pure spirit and wanted to have a baby without touching a man.
Sarah wanted a divine child created of cosmic energy.
As a six-year-old, Sarah insisted that all living things came directly from God and from a special place we could not see.
Alex Goddard states that Sarah was born with an abnormality of the uterus.
The uterine abnormality is very rare, afflicting only about one woman in twenty thousand.
Sarah refused to give up despite the diagnosis, and Goddard describes her as a person of enormous tenacity.
Sarah declared she wanted to come to Baalum, the place of miracles.
Goddard told Sarah that miracles can sometimes transpire at Baalum but only at a great price.
Goddard said an agreement would be required and Sarah would have to keep it no matter what.
Goddard later regretted the offer, judging Sarah far too unstable for the Baalum environment.
Goddard forbade Sarah to come, but she found out about his next scheduled trip and booked herself passage.
The narrator first met Goddard on a morning overlooking the bluffs of the Hudson.
The narrator notes that she and Sarah had sought miracles from Goddard for similar reasons.
The narrator feels guilt over Sarah, reflecting that Sarah should have come home to her and to Lou.

entities.name: Alex Goddard
entities.role: Man who worked with Sarah on her pregnancy hopes, diagnosed her uterine abnormality, and offered her a conditional trip to Baalum

entities.name: Sarah
entities.role: Troubled young woman seeking a virgin-birth miracle who insisted on going to Baalum despite being forbidden

entities.name: Quetzal Manor
entities.role: Location in New York where Sarah first appeared seeking help

entities.name: Baalum
entities.role: Place of miracles, where Sarah wanted to go and where Goddard's work occurs

entities.name: Lou
entities.role: Family member whom the narrator and Sarah both loved; Sarah should have come home to Lou and the narrator
